name: Tortoise
label: Thrill Jockey
lede: Tortoise runs two bassists, three drummers who also play vibraphone and marimba, and no singer. Chicago gave the band a genre name it never wanted, and thirty years of records have kept outrunning it.

eras.title: A rhythm section for hire turns into a band
eras.text: Doug McCombs of Eleventh Dream Day and drummer John Herndon meant to be a freelance rhythm section, Chicago's answer to Sly and Robbie. Instead they gathered drummers and bassists from the city's noise and art-rock bands until the thing needed a name.

years.h: Doug McCombs and John Herndon plan to be Chicago's Sly and Robbie
years.p: McCombs, bassist of [[Eleventh Dream Day|751b1385-9595-46ee-b634-8f90f892682a]], and drummer Herndon set out as a freelance rhythm section modeled on the Jamaican duo. The plan turns into a band.

years.src: Wikipedia: John McEntire · Wikipedia: Bundy K. Brown
years.h: John McEntire and Bundy K. Brown join the group, then called Mosquito
years.p: Two veterans of [[Bastro|cfc5b1bf-a46c-4504-bcb6-a820416a1894]] and [[Gastr del Sol|8f54d90b-f322-4e5d-a0fd-bdc960f2d20f]] come aboard: McEntire on drums and studio know-how, Brown on bass. The name Tortoise comes later.
years.xp: McEntire had studied percussion and then the new music technology program at Oberlin Conservatory, played in Bastro with [[David Grubbs|f72e65e9-3ee7-4dce-9c53-5dc6221f6cd3]], and moved to Chicago in 1991. Brown had replaced Bastro's bassist in 1990 and went on to form Gastr del Sol with Grubbs.

years.h: Dan Bitney makes three drummers
years.p: Percussionist [[Dan Bitney|781f0356-33b7-4168-8f68-db9387063320]] arrives. Tortoise is now two bass players plus three people who swap between drums, vibraphone and marimba.

years.h: The first single arrives a year before the first album
years.p: Tortoise issues its first single in 1993, ahead of any album.

years.h: A week in November produces the whole debut
years.p: Between November 29 and December 5, 1993, the five members cut ten instrumentals, with McEntire recording and mixing.

eras.title: A genre nobody in the band asked for
eras.text: The debut came out on Thrill Jockey, a two-year-old label run by ex-Atlantic A&R woman Bettina Richards, and critics went looking for a word. They found post-rock. Tortoise has been saying no thanks ever since.

years.h: Tortoise arrives on Thrill Jockey in a Sam Prekop sleeve
years.p: Ten collaborative instrumentals of mid-tempo dub, rusted guitar and mallets, with a cover by [[Sam Prekop|33175dbe-db6c-4f0b-a4c6-9addcd403186]] of [[The Sea and Cake|74171cb6-1ff8-42bd-be8a-96660c22e3e0]]. By March 1998 it had sold about 35,000 copies, according to Wikipedia.
years.xp: AllMusic's Glenn Swan praised its meditative grooves and rusty guitar-string ambience. Of those 35,000 copies, about 8,000 were vinyl and 27,000 CDs.

years.h: Simon Reynolds defines post-rock, and Tortoise ends up wearing it
years.p: Simon Reynolds's definition in The Wire, May 1994. Tortoise becomes the genre's poster band and the band rejects the label.
years.xp:
Reynolds's full definition: "using rock instrumentation for non-rock purposes, using guitars as facilitators of timbre and textures rather than riffs and power chords." He first used the term in Melody Maker in late 1993 and in a March 1994 Mojo review of Bark Psychosis. Two years later, Millions Now Living Will Never Die made it stick to Tortoise.

The band rejected it, arguing that one word for so many styles robbed it of its individuality. [[Mogwai|d700b3f5-45af-4d02-95ed-57d301bda93e]], [[Godspeed You! Black Emperor|3648db01-b29d-4ab9-835c-83f6a5068fe4]] and Cul de Sac distanced themselves from the label for the same reason.

years.h: Bundy K. Brown quits after one album but stays close
years.p: Brown remixes the band and later forms Pullman with McCombs.

years.h: Rhythms, Resolutions & Clusters hands the debut to remixers
years.p: Friends including [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] and [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]] take the first album apart, an early sign Tortoise treats its own records as raw material.

years.h: David Pajo of Slint takes Brown's place
years.p: The guitarist and bassist from Louisville's [[Slint|2869c510-2679-4a3f-bf15-e5e8b49f2f28]] replaces Bundy K. Brown.

years.h: June sessions at Idful and Soma begin the second album
years.p: Tortoise records Millions Now Living Will Never Die from June to September 1995, at Idful and at McEntire's Soma studio in Chicago's Wicker Park.

eras.title: Record of the year, without a word sung
eras.text: A twenty-one-minute opening track made Millions Now Living Will Never Die the record critics measured others against. Then Jeff Parker arrived from Chicago's jazz scene and the band rebuilt itself inside a computer.

q: two or three different ideas for songs and then smash them together
years.src: Wikipedia: Millions Now Living Will Never Die · Wikipedia: Tortoise (band)
years.h: Millions Now Living Will Never Die opens with 21 minutes of Djed
years.p: Tortoise's second album leads with Djed, 20 minutes 57 seconds of shifting sections. The title is a 1920s Jehovah's Witnesses slogan, used by Joseph Franklin Rutherford.
years.xp:
The Taut and Tame was co-written with the departed Bundy K. Brown, and Dear Grandma and Grandpa samples the German band Dom's 1972 track Silence. John McEntire recorded and mixed it.

By March 1998 it had sold over 50,000 copies, about 80 percent of them on CD, and it reached number 115 in the UK.

years.h: Trans Am's debut lands the same day, produced by McEntire
years.p: Thrill Jockey releases [[Trans Am|7c5acaaa-3f74-4e16-82b2-f8046fce4338]]'s first album the day Millions comes out. McEntire produced it, and Trans Am goes on to open for Tortoise on a US tour.

years.h: Tortoise contributes to the Red Hot AIDS benefit Offbeat
years.p: Offbeat: A Red Hot Soundtrip is a Red Hot Organization benefit album, and Tortoise is on it.

years.h: Japan gets a compendium nobody else does
years.p: A Digest Compendium of the Tortoise's World gathers debut tracks, remixes and singles, released in Japan only.

years.h: Jeff Parker brings Chicago jazz in on guitar
years.p: Parker, of [[Isotope 217|534614e7-957c-420a-9d81-6239a471e1c7]] and the Chicago Underground Trio, becomes Tortoise's second guitarist.

years.src: Wikipedia: Millions Now Living Will Never Die
years.h: The Wire's critics vote Millions record of the year
years.p: Tortoise's second album tops the British magazine's poll for 1996. NME ranks it 35th.
years.xp:
Reviews were strong: Alternative Press gave it 5 out of 5, Uncut 9 out of 10 and NME 8 out of 10. The Village Voice was cooler, with a B-minus.

It later turned up in the book 1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die.

years.h: TNT gets built one overdub at a time
years.p: From November 1996 to November 1997 the band assembles its jazziest record on hard disk. The cover is a doodle a member drew on a CD-R insert during the sessions.
years.xp:
McEntire has described the method as piecemeal and forward-then-back, with every element overdubbed. Violin, cornet, bassoon, trombone and cello were used for color, not solos.

Pitchfork gave it 9.0 and The New York Times ranked it fifth of 1998. NME's James Oldham dissented, calling it an admirable collection that says nothing.

years.h: David Pajo quits to go solo as Aerial M
years.p: With TNT finished, he concentrates on the project that later becomes Papa M.

years.h: Remixed collects the TNT-era remixes
years.p: A second remix set; the 2001 reissue adds a remix by [[Autechre|410c9baf-5469-44f6-9852-826524b80c61]].

eras.title: Back in the room
eras.text: After TNT was assembled on hard disk, Tortoise moved into a bigger Soma and played together again. Reviews split, and in 2006 the band backed Bonnie 'Prince' Billy on a set of other people's songs.

years.h: Standards gets a Midwest tryout before the studio
years.p: Tortoise demos the songs, plays them live around Madison, Milwaukee and Champaign, then records together in Soma's newly expanded room. Pitchfork gives it 9.2.
years.xp: Eden 1 and Eden 2 go back to the TNT sessions, and Firefly slides from the studio take into a band practice recording. It reached number 200 on the Billboard 200.

years.h: Ellington's Didjeridoo gets a Tortoise cover for Red Hot + Indigo
years.p: Red Hot + Indigo is the Red Hot Organization's tribute to Duke Ellington.

yt: Live at Mississippi Nights, St. Louis, 2001
years.h: Tortoise picks the lineup for All Tomorrow's Parties
years.p: The band curates an edition of the British festival in 2001, and another day in 2004.

years.src: Wikipedia: It's All Around You · Michigan Daily
years.h: It's All Around You earns a 5.2 from Pitchfork
years.p: The first album with the settled five of Bitney, Herndon, McCombs, McEntire and Parker splits critics. In 2011 rapper Currensy lists it among his 25 favorite albums.
years.xp: Currensy called it an acid trip in audio form. Herndon, asked about the band's reputation that year, told the Michigan Daily: "I think people have this idea that we're overly serious about what we do, but we bring humor as well."

years.src: Wikipedia: The Brave and the Bold (album)
years.h: Bonnie 'Prince' Billy sings Springsteen, Devo and Lungfish over Tortoise
years.p: The Brave and the Bold, cut at Soma in 2003 and 2004, puts Will Oldham's voice over Tortoise on ten covers, from the [[Minutemen|d4ad0149-d8ae-4105-8009-0221fce9ff35]] and Elton John to Milton Nascimento.
years.xp: Released by Overcoat Recordings, it also covers Don Williams, Melanie, Richard Thompson and Quix*o*tic. Pitchfork's Amanda Petrusich was unmoved; PopMatters heard a melding of minds.

years.h: A Lazarus Taxon boxes up the singles and remixes
years.p: Two CDs of singles and remixes, an expanded Rhythms, Resolutions & Clusters and a DVD of videos and live footage.

years.h: ATP's Don't Look Back series gets Millions in full
years.p: At All Tomorrow's Parties in 2006, Tortoise performs the 1996 album start to finish. It does the same again in 2008.

eras.title: Commissioned by the city
eras.text: Tortoise got a radio station in Grand Theft Auto, a horror-film score and a Beck experiment. Then Chicago commissioned a suite, and the record took six years.

years.h: Grand Theft Auto gets a Tortoise radio station
years.p: The iOS, Android and PSP versions of Grand Theft Auto: Chinatown Wars carry a dedicated Tortoise station.

years.h: Beacons of Ancestorship ends a five-year gap
years.p: Tortoise's sixth album reaches 149 on the Billboard 200. The band tours the Midwest in the fall and Europe through December.

years.h: Beck's Record Club has Tortoise remake Yanni's Acropolis concert
years.p: Tortoise joins [[Beck|309c62ba-7a22-4277-9f67-4a162526d18a]], [[Thurston Moore|8ba48525-d922-42ee-9775-97b7b8f9712e]] and Brian LeBarton for the online series, redoing the new age album Yanni Live at the Acropolis.

years.cap: Tortoise at the Lincoln Theatre, Raleigh, North Carolina, September 12, 2010
years.h: ATP New York in the Catskills books Tortoise
years.p: The band appears at the festival's 2010 New York edition in Monticello.

years.h: Eduardo Sánchez's horror film Lovely Molly gets a Tortoise score
years.p: The band writes and records the soundtrack to Eduardo Sánchez's psychological horror film, inspired by traditional folk songs.

years.cap: Tortoise live in Santiago de Compostela, Spain
years.h: Jeff Parker moves to Los Angeles, and the band spans two cities
years.p: The Los Angeles Times covers the move. Tortoise now lives in two cities, and later three.

q: the obvious solution to begin with was to take those pieces
years.src: Thrill Jockey: Tortoise · Wikipedia: The Catastrophist
years.h: A City of Chicago commission turns into The Catastrophist
years.p: In 2010 the city commissions a suite drawing on its jazz and improv scenes. It becomes Tortoise's first album since 2009, with guest singers.
years.xp:
[[Todd Rittmann|44064fd6-ec2c-4325-950e-1a00b656252c]] of [[U.S. Maple|6a340e0b-5022-4a2b-bc7d-98f6aa07495f]] sings David Essex's Rock On, and [[Georgia Hubley|c1a639ae-ebba-4f47-9a4b-937167a5295f]] of [[Yo La Tengo|3f542031-b054-454d-b57b-812fa2a81b11]] sings the new ballad Yonder Blue. Parker said every song went through intensive restructuring, and plenty was shelved.

McEntire said the commission pieces started as just heads and solos before they were orchestrated. Pitchfork gave it 6.8 and Metacritic scored it 73.

eras.title: Nine years, three cities
eras.text: By the 2020s the members lived in Chicago, Los Angeles and Portland, and McEntire had moved Soma from Wicker Park to Oregon in 2019. They made a record anyway, on a new label.

years.src: Wikipedia: Touch (Tortoise album) · Wikipedia: John McEntire
years.h: Touch arrives nine years after the last record
years.p: Tortoise records in Portland, Los Angeles and at [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]]'s Electrical Audio in Chicago. It comes out on International Anthem and Nonesuch, and The Wire puts it tenth among its 2025 releases.
years.xp:
Sessions ran at Flora Recording & Playback in Portland, 64 Sound in Los Angeles and Electrical Audio, with McEntire recording and mixing. Lead single Oganesson came out on March 27, 2025.

Metacritic scored it 81 and Pitchfork gave it 7.6. PopMatters called it "A cinematic record that is profoundly human and entirely spectral." Not everyone was sold: The Quietus heard clashing elements and bland production, and Exclaim! wrote that the band carried the burden of its back catalogue.
